subject: Non integer values for multinomial likelihood

messages.author: c02e0f9087e29020
messages.subject: Non integer values for multinomial likelihood
parts:
Hi, I am looking to use a multinomial likelihood with data that are weighted and therefore non-integer. From the definition of the multinomial in the manual it suggests it only takes integer values. 

Instead (again, based on what I see in the manual), it looks like I should increment lp__ by the relevant part of the log likelihood:

for(i in 1:N) {
 lp__ <- lp__ + log( theta[i] ) * y[i]
 }

Where theta is a simplex of N components, and y is my vector of observed (weighted) data, with N components.

Does this look correct?  Sorry for the nube question, but I assume lp__ is something I could happily mess up and not notice.

Thanks - Nick

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Non integer values for multinomial likelihood
parts:
On 9/19/13 11:09 PM, Nick Menzies wrote:
>
> Hi, I am looking to use a multinomial likelihood with data that are weighted and therefore non-integer. From the
> definition of the multinomial in the manual it suggests it only takes integer values.
Right. It only takes integers.

> Instead (again, based on what I see in the manual), it looks like I should increment lp__ by the relevant part of the
> log likelihood:
>
> for(i in 1:N) {
> lp__ <- lp__ + log( theta[i] ) * y[i]
> }

Yes, this will treat

p(theta) propto PRODUCT_{i in 1:N} theta[i]^y[i]

But I don't think it'll normalize properly over the continuous support.

You'll see that it has the same kernel density as the Dirichlet
distribution (the conjugate prior, so not surprising), though you'll also
see an off-by-one term there. And you can see the gamma functions required
to normalize it.

> Where theta is a simplex of N components, and y is my vector of observed (weighted) data, with N components.
>
> Does this look correct? Sorry for the nube question, but I assume lp__ is something I could happily mess up and not notice.

Yes, it's tricky. Not so much that lp__ itself is tricky,
but that it's tricky to define density functions properly.

- Bob

messages.author: c02e0f9087e29020
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Non integer values for multinomial likelihood
parts:
Hi Bob -- thanks for this. Just so I understand, you are suggesting that this likelihood can be achieved by:

theta ~ dirichlet(y)

or alternately: 

 lp__ <- lp__ + log( theta ) * y + lgamma( sum( y ) ) - sum( lgamma( y ) )
 
Where y is my vector of non-integer count data and theta is my simplex.

I should also assume the former will be faster, correct?

Thanks - Nick

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Non integer values for multinomial likelihood
parts:
I'm not exactly sure what the effect will be either way
or which one is the "right" one to deal with approximate
count data. Someone should know...

I was just saying that as a continuous density it's
not properly normalized (doesn't integrate to 1).

You would need to use the the sum of elementwise products

sum(log(theta) .* y)

Your version (as amended above) will probably be faster
because (a) you don't need to fiddle with the subtraction of 1 you
see in the Dirichlet definition, and (b) our Dirichlet implementation
isn't vectorized (in case you had multiple theta). You do lose
error checking (parameter y must be positive and theta must be
a simplex --- you do get a check for dimensions matching in the .*).

- Bob
